root_idea.summary: The root centers on the bodily substance or bodily person of a thing, distinct from its extremities.
root_idea.development: From the notion of bodily mass or substantial form, the lexicon develops meanings of corporeality, bodily largeness and fatness, age-related bulk, the sacrificial animal named for its size or fattening, and body-covering armor.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized noun citation form بَدَنٌ.
The Quranic plural بُدْنَ is displayed under the supported singular dictionary citation form بَدَنَةٌ.

senses.definition: The body or bodily person, especially the corporeal body distinguished from the soul.
senses.usage_conditions: In 10:92, ببدنك refers to the body rather than the living person; the lexical interpretation includes a body left without the soul.

senses.definition: A coat of mail or other short body-covering armor.
senses.usage_conditions: An attested alternative interpretation of ببدنك in 10:92; the term is also used for armor or a garment that covers the body.

senses.definition: A sacrificial camel, and by established sacrificial usage also a cow or bull; in the Quranic plural, the animals offered as sacrifice.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural بُدْنَ, referring to sacrificial animals brought or offered for the rite. The lexical evidence distinguishes this term from sheep and goats.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become big-bodied, bulky, corpulent, or fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verb used of a man or a camel; بَدَنَ is also reported as a variant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become aged, weak, or heavy through age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The aging sense is distinguished from simple bodily corpulence in the lexical evidence.
A classical usage of the Form II verb, alongside the reported aging sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fatness and compactness; fat or adipose substance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a nominal meaning distinct from the plural use of بُدْنٌ for a sacrificial animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The body or central panel of a shirt or jubba, lying against the back and belly without sleeves or gores; by extension, a small jubba.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A garment-related use derived from the body's central covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In شِرْكَةُ الأَبْدَانِ, bodily partnership or copartnership in physical labor for earning gains.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional commercial or legal expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A limb or member, especially the limbs of a slaughtered camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized application of the body term.
Used adjectivally of a person characterized as aged.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An old mountain goat or ibex.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological use for an aged mountain goat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lineage or parentage of a man, including the grounds of his claim to respect or honor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from bodily identity to ancestry and social standing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of or relating to the body; corporeal.
Big-bodied, bulky, corpulent, or fat; heavy in body, including heaviness due to age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing bodily size or heaviness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One that becomes fat quickly despite little fodder or food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive noun for an animal or person that gains fat readily.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The coat-of-mail construction is covered by the Quran-attested armor sense.
Plural-form relation to بَدَنَةٌ; no independent lexical meaning.
Plural-form relation to بَادِنٌ; no independent lexical meaning.
The small-jubba use belongs to the same garment branch.
Plural-form relation to بَدَنَةٌ; no independent lexical meaning.

cautions: The Quranic interpretation of ببدنك in 10:92 is reported both as the body and as a coat of mail; these are retained as separate Quranic senses.
The public headword بَدَنَةٌ is the singular citation form for the Quranic plural بُدْنَ. Classical usage also records بُدْنٌ as a plural of بَادِنٌ, but the Quranic context is sacrificial.
Classical evidence varies over whether بَدَنَةٌ includes male camels and bovines; the entry reflects the attested camel, cow, and bull range and the explicit exclusion of sheep and goats.
